chapters.title: Faith, and the saying of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: “Islam is built on five”
Matters of faith
The Muslim is one from whose tongue and hand the Muslims are safe
Whose Islam is best?
Feeding people is part of Islam
Loving for one’s brother what one loves for oneself is part of faith
Love for the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is part of faith
The sweetness of faith
Love for the Ansar is a sign of faith
Chapter
Fleeing from trials is part of religion
The saying of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: “I am the most knowledgeable of Allah among you”
Hating to return to disbelief as one hates to be thrown into the Fire is part of faith
The differing degrees of the people of faith in deeds
Modesty is part of faith
“If they repent, establish prayer and give zakat, then let them go on their way”
Those who say that faith is action

When Islam is not genuine, but is submission or fear of being killed, because of His saying: {The desert Arabs say, “We believe.” Say, “You have not believed, but say, ‘We have submitted.’”} When it is genuine, it is according to His saying, exalted is His mention: {Indeed, religion with Allah is Islam}
Spreading the greeting of peace is part of Islam
Chapter heading under review

license.attribution: Sahih al-Bukhari by Muhammad ibn Ismail al-Bukhari; Arabic digital transcription by Arabic Wikisource contributors, opening revision 484874 and Faith revision 490285.
license.changes: Entries 1–2 are unchanged. Entries 3–7 are derived from the pinned Arabic; Hadith 5 has one explicitly recorded correction from له to لك supported by two printed witnesses. Original inputs are retained in prototype-inputs.json. New AI-assisted English, presentation and comparison notes are offered under CC BY-SA 4.0. This does not license third-party comparison translations or the rest of the app. Hadith 8–29 retain their Arabic paragraphs unchanged from revision 490285; their new English and available chapter titles are AI-assisted. A disputed chapter heading is explicitly withheld. Chapter introductions are preserved separately in Arabic, with English translation still pending.

findings: The selected digital Arabic includes full chains of transmission; the working English retains them.

The Brill print abbreviates the first narrator to al-Humaydi while the selected digital text and Darussalam give his name. Honorific wording and orthography also differ. These are recorded as witness differences, not silently harmonized.

The first two narration bodies were visually compared against the Darussalam Arabic and the older print. No additional substantive body clause was identified in those comparisons. This is an AI review, not an independent human audit.
The sample and a digital edition are not presumed identical merely because their translator is the same.
A close translation still involves linguistic judgment; zero interpretation and infallibility cannot honestly be promised.
Entries 3–7 have AI comparison records and declared wording choices; no human accuracy certification is claimed. The derived Hadith 5 correction does not modify the pinned digital input.

arabic_blocks: [8] حدثنا عبيد الله بن موسى قال: أخبرنا حنظلة بن أبي سفيان عن عكرمة بن خالد عن ابن عمر رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ:
بني الإسلام على خمس شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله وأن محمدا رسول الله وإقام الصلاة وإيتاء الزكاة والحج وصوم رمضان.
english_blocks: ‘Ubaydullah ibn Musa related to us: Hanzalah ibn Abi Sufyan informed us, from ‘Ikrimah ibn Khalid, from Ibn ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:
“Islam is built on five: testifying that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, establishing prayer, giving zakat, pilgrimage, and fasting Ramadan.”
entries.english_status: Personal prototype: AI-assisted working translation; two Arabic printed witnesses and two English translation families compared. Independent Arabic, English and context review pending.

notes: Keep all five elements in the selected order, with pilgrimage before fasting. Neither explanatory conditions on prayer nor a destination gloss is inserted.
Both English comparisons retain the five-part structure; their explanatory additions are not part of this Arabic input.
review.reviewScope: Every selected Arabic paragraph, full chain, narration and any final transmission note was compared with the two printed witnesses. English body comparisons use two named translation families; their abridged chains do not independently verify the full English chain.

arabic_blocks: [9] حدثنا عبد الله بن محمد قال: حدثنا أبو عامر العقدي قال: حدثنا سليمان بن بلال عن عبد الله بن دينار عن أبي صالح عن أبي هريرة رضى الله تعالى عنه عن النبي ﷺ قال:
الإيمان بضع وستون شعبة والحياء شعبة من الإيمان.
english_blocks: ‘Abdullah ibn Muhammad related to us: Abu ‘Amir al-‘Aqadi related to us: Sulayman ibn Bilal related to us, from ‘Abdullah ibn Dinar, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:
“Faith has more than sixty branches, and modesty is a branch of faith.”
entries.english_status: Personal prototype: AI-assisted working translation; two Arabic printed witnesses and two English translation families compared. Independent Arabic, English and context review pending.

notes: Render bida‘ wa-sittun as more than sixty; do not replace it with the seventy-branch wording of another transmission. Modesty is the working equivalent for haya’, whose semantic range is wider than embarrassment.
The two English comparisons agree on the sixty range. The Khan-family version additionally explains haya’.
review.reviewScope: Every selected Arabic paragraph, full chain, narration and any final transmission note was compared with the two printed witnesses. English body comparisons use two named translation families; their abridged chains do not independently verify the full English chain.

arabic_blocks: [10] حدثنا آدم بن أبي إياس قال: حدثنا شعبة عن عبد الله بن أبي السفر وإسماعيل عن الشعبي عن عبد الله بن عمرو رضى الله تعالى عنهما عن النبي ﷺ قال:
المسلم من سلم المسلمون من لسانه ويده والمهاجر من هجر ما نهى الله عنه
قال أبو عبد الله، وقال أبو معاوية حدثنا داود عن عامر قال: سمعت عبد الله عن النبي ﷺ، وقال عبد الأعلى عن داود عن عامر عن عبد الله عن النبي ﷺ.

أن رسول الله ﷺ قال: وحوله عصابة من أصحابه بايعوني على أن لا تشركوا بالله شيئا ولا تسرقوا ولا تزنوا ولا تقتلوا أولادكم ولا تأتوا ببهتان تفترونه بين أيديكم وأرجلكم ولا تعصوا في معروف فمن وفي منكم فأجره على الله ومن أصاب من ذلك شيئا فعوقب في الدنيا فهو كفارة له ومن أصاب من ذلك شيئا ثم ستره الله فهو إلى الله إن شاء عفا عنه وإن شاء عاقبه فبايعناه على ذلك.

Whoever among you fulfils this, his reward rests with Allah. Whoever commits any of these things and is punished in this world, that is an expiation for him. Whoever commits any of these things and Allah then conceals it, his affair rests with Allah: if He wills, He pardons him, and if He wills, He punishes him.” So we pledged allegiance to him on that basis.

arabic_blocks: [25] حدثنا عبد الله بن محمد المسندي قال: حدثنا أبو روح الحرمي بن عمارة قال: حدثنا شعبة عن واقد بن محمد قال: سمعت أبي يحدث عن ابن عمر أن رسول الله ﷺ قال:
أمرت أن أقاتل الناس حتى يشهدوا أن لا إله إلا الله وأن محمدا رسول الله ويقيموا الصلاة ويؤتوا الزكاة فإذا فعلوا ذلك عصموا مني دماءهم وأموالهم إلا بحق الإسلام وحسابهم على الله.
english_blocks: ‘Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Musnadi related to us: Abu Ruh al-Harami ibn ‘Umarah related to us: Shu‘bah related to us, from Waqid ibn Muhammad, who said: I heard my father relate from Ibn ‘Umar that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“I have been commanded to fight the people until they testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, establish prayer, and give zakat. When they do that, they protect their blood and property from me, except by the right of Islam, and their reckoning rests with Allah.”
entries.english_status: Personal prototype: AI-assisted working translation; two Arabic printed witnesses and two English translation families compared. Independent Arabic, English and context review pending.

notes: The full chain, testimony, prayer, zakat, protection clause, exception and final reckoning clause are preserved. The working translation does not add a legal application or replace the general source wording with a narrower group.

The historical print has fa-qad before the protection clause; the selected digital and modern print do not. The chapter’s Qur’anic quotation is separate from the numbered hadith. The English comparisons supply some explanatory wording; it is not imported.

arabic_blocks: [26] حدثنا أحمد بن يونس وموسى بن إسماعيل قالا: حدثنا إبراهيم بن سعد قال: حدثنا ابن شهاب عن سعيد بن المسيب عن أبي هريرة:
أن رسول الله ﷺ سئل أي العمل أفضل، فقال إيمان بالله ورسوله قيل ثم ماذا قال الجهاد في سبيل الله قيل ثم ماذا قال حج مبرور
english_blocks: Ahmad ibn Yunus and Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us. They said: Ibrahim ibn Sa‘d related to us: Ibn Shihab related to us, from Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was asked, “Which deed is best?” He said, “Faith in Allah and His Messenger.” It was asked, “Then what?” He said, “Jihad in Allah’s path.” It was asked, “Then what?” He said, “An accepted Hajj.”
entries.english_status: Personal prototype: AI-assisted working translation; two Arabic printed witnesses and two English translation families compared. Independent Arabic, English and context review pending.

notes: The two opening transmitters and the joint ‘they said’ are retained. The three questions and answers remain in order.

Jihad is retained as the source term, and mabrur is provisionally rendered ‘accepted’. The Khan-family comparison expands both with explanatory conditions; those additions are not part of the selected Arabic and are not inserted.

arabic_blocks: [27] حدثنا أبو اليمان قال: أخبرنا شعيب عن الزهري قال: أخبرني عامر بن سعد بن أبي وقاص عن سعد رضى الله تعالى عنه أن رسول الله ﷺ:

أعطى رهطا وسعد جالس فترك رسول الله ﷺ رجلا هو أعجبهم إلي فقلت: يا رسول الله مالك عن فلان فوالله إني لأراه مؤمنا، فقال أو مسلما فسكت قليلا ثم غلبني ما أعلم منه فعدت لمقالتي فقلت: مالك عن فلان فوالله إني لأراه مؤمنا، فقال أو مسلما ثم غلبني ما أعلم منه فعدت لمقالتي وعاد رسول الله ﷺ، ثم قال: يا سعد إني لأعطي الرجل وغيره أحب إلي منه خشية أن يكبه الله في النار .
ورواه يونس وصالح ومعمر وابن أخي الزهري عن الزهري.
english_blocks: Abu al-Yaman related to us: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: ‘Amir ibn Sa‘d ibn Abi Waqqas informed me, from Sa‘d, may Allah Most High be pleased with him:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, gave to a group of men while Sa‘d was sitting there. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, left out a man who was the one I admired most. I said, “Messenger of Allah, why have you passed over so-and-so? By Allah, I regard him as a believer.” He said, “Or a Muslim.” I was silent for a little while, but then what I knew about him overcame me, and I repeated my words. I said, “Why have you passed over so-and-so? By Allah, I regard him as a believer.” He said, “Or a Muslim.” Then what I knew about him overcame me, and I repeated my words, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, repeated his. Then he said, “Sa‘d, I give to a man while another is dearer to me than he is, for fear that Allah may cast him headlong into the Fire.”
Yunus, Salih, Ma‘mar and the son of al-Zuhri’s brother also related it from al-Zuhri.

notes: The report retains the move from third-person Sa‘d to first-person narration, the repeated exchange and the final explanation. ‘Or a Muslim’ is not expanded with ‘merely’ or ‘just’, which appear in the English comparisons but not as separate words in the Arabic.
The historical print repeats ‘I was silent for a little while’ after the second reply. The selected digital and modern print do not contain that second pause, so it is not added.

The final alternate-transmission note is preserved separately and in full. The Khan-family comparison omits it; Bewley and both Arabic printed witnesses include it. The word zakat supplied by the Khan-family comparison is not in the selected body and is not inserted.
At ‘Amir’s reporting verb, the modern print has akhbarana, while the selected digital and historical print have akhbarani. The selected ‘informed me’ is retained.

For a complete opening sentence when the chain is collapsed, the English Messenger clause from the end of the first Arabic paragraph opens the following English body paragraph. Its words and honorific occur once; the Arabic paragraph and source order are unchanged.

arabic_blocks: [28] حدثنا قتيبة قال: حدثنا الليث عن يزيد بن أبي حبيب عن أبي الخير عن عبد الله بن عمرو أن رجلا سأل رسول الله ﷺ:
أي الإسلام خير قال تطعم الطعام وتقرأ السلام على من عرفت ومن لم تعرف.
english_blocks: Qutaybah related to us: al-Layth related to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Abu al-Khayr, from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr:
A man asked the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:
“Which aspect of Islam is best?” He said, “You feed people and offer the greeting of peace to those you know and those you do not know.”

notes: This is a separate source record from Hadith 12, with a different full chain. It is not deduplicated or substituted with the earlier entry.
The greeting is offered both to people known and unknown. The Khan-family supplied restriction ‘the poor’ after feeding is not added because it is absent from the selected Arabic.

arabic_blocks: [29] حدثنا عبد الله بن مسلمة عن مالك عن زيد بن أسلم عن عطاء بن يسار عن ابن عباس قال: قال النبي ﷺ:
أريت النار فإذا أكثر أهلها النساء يكفرن قيل أيكفرن بالله قال يكفرن العشير ويكفرن الإحسان لو أحسنت إلى إحداهن الدهر ثم رأت منك شيئا قالت ما رأيت منك خيرا قط.
english_blocks: ‘Abdullah ibn Maslamah related to us, from Malik, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from ‘Ata’ ibn Yasar, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“I was shown the Fire, and most of its inhabitants were women who were ungrateful.” It was asked, “Do they disbelieve in Allah?” He said, “They are ungrateful to their husbands and ungrateful for kindness. If you were to be kind to one of them for a lifetime, then she saw something from you, she would say, ‘I have never seen any good from you.’”
entries.english_status: Personal prototype: AI-assisted working translation; two Arabic printed witnesses and two English translation families compared. Independent Arabic, English and context review pending.

notes: The repeated Arabic kufr-root wording moves between ingratitude and disbelief in the question and answer. The working English uses ‘ungrateful’ in the first statement and the explanation, and ‘disbelieve’ in the question, following the distinction also discussed by both English comparisons.

The chapter heading differs: the digital source reads ‘وكفر بعد كفر فيه’, while both inspected prints read ‘وكفر دون كفر’ before the separate connective fi-hi. The English heading is withheld as ‘Chapter heading under review’; the exact digital heading and its following context are preserved. This is not an applied correction to the Arabic.
The report body, including the lifelong kindness and the concluding denial, was checked separately from the heading discrepancy. No claim about present-day people or a legal application is added.
